newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece not targeting FX index - c. bank official.
newsitem.headline: Greece not targeting FX index - c. bank official.

text.p: Greece's central bank has not formed and targeted a trade-weighted foreign exchange index containing the currencies that make up the ecu, a high-level central bank official told Reuters.

A Sunday press report said the central bank would target a basket of currencies that make up the ecu but with different weights defined by the magnitude of trade flows between Greece and other EU countries.
However, the official said no such index was mentioned in the central bank governor's policy speech on Friday and thus, no such index was being followed.
Instead, he reiterated that 1997 forex policy will remain focused on fighting inflation and that the drachma will be stable but more flexible versus currencies making up the ecu.

"The main goal of the foreign exchange policy is to combat inflation," the official said. "As the governor stated on Friday, the drachma will be stable but more flexible versus the main currencies that make up the ecu."
The central bank official said the magnitude of trade flows between Greece and other EU countries defined the main currencies that make up the ecu.
"We, at the central bank, place great importance on credibility and we intend to preserve it," the official added. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
